name: Maatchaa
tagline: Matches Shopify products with trending YouTube Shorts so brands can swipe through creator sponsorships.
problem: Short-form creators want sponsors and brands want new audiences, but finding the right creator–product pairs and setting up each deal is manual work.
solution: Videos are turned into text and thumbnails, embedded alongside a store's Shopify catalog in a vector database, and matched to products; businesses browse candidate creators in a swipe-style dashboard, and once a creator accepts, the tool generates a product-set image and updates the video description through the YouTube API.
demo_moment: Team-described: a business swipes through Shorts already matched to its own products, and an accepted deal updates the creator's video automatically.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Selected by the organizer as one of 12 finalists among 261 submissions.
Serves both sides of a sponsorship: businesses find creators, and creators get the deal set up for them.
Used an image model released shortly before the event to generate the product sets.
The swipe interface borrows a pattern every judge already knows, so the matching engine needs no explanation.

lessons: Wrap a matching engine in a gesture people already use (swiping) and the demo explains itself.
